study_identification_part.si4_title: Linking Personalized Brain Atrophy to Schizophrenia Network and Treatment Response

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To test whether personalized brain atrophy maps for individuals with schizophrenia comprise a disorder-specific functional brain network and explain individual variation in clinical response to repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS).

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Pearson's correlations between personalized atrophy network connectivity at rTMS target and PANSS improvement (baseline minus post-rTMS scores divided by baseline); linear mixed-effect models for treatment effects (Time × Group interaction); spin-based spatial correlation tests with permutation correction (10,000 permutations) for brain map comparisons across HCP-MMP atlas ROIs; permutation-based two-sample t-test (FSL PALM, 10,000 permutations, TFCE, PFWE < .001) for specificity analysis comparing schizophrenia vs non-psychiatric disorder atrophy networks; partial correlation controlling for age, gender, education, HAMA, HAMD, and disease duration.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Personalized atrophy maps were highly heterogeneous across patients but functionally converged to a common schizophrenia network (MPFC, insula); connectivity between personalized atrophy networks and rTMS targets significantly predicted treatment response (r = 0.54, P = .005 for active rTMS).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: The study identified vertex-wise cortical thickness deviations for 91 schizophrenia patients using normative modeling based on 797 healthy controls. All 91 patients showed atrophy loci (W > 2), with highest structural overlap of 46% in the right insular cortex. Despite heterogeneous atrophy locations, 88% of patients showed functional connectivity convergence in bilateral medial prefrontal cortex (MPFC). This personalized atrophy network was spatially correlated (r = 0.67, Pspin < .0001) with schizophrenia networks derived from 27 case-control contrasts in the literature. In the rTMS subset (n = 52), active rTMS significantly reduced PANSS scores (from 73.4 ± 18.34 to 57.7 ± 13.39, P < .0001) while sham showed no change. Critically, connectivity strength of the rTMS target (left TPJ) within each patient's personalized atrophy network significantly predicted symptom improvement (r = 0.54, P = .005; r = 0.56, P = .01 after controlling for covariates), but only for active stimulation (not sham: r = 0.25, P = .24).

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Single-center normative model may not generalize to other centers; exclusive focus on schizophrenia (not tested in other psychiatric disorders); results based on inhibitory rTMS only; overlap ratio of personalized atrophy maps not directly comparable to atrophy network maps due to different sparsity levels.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: "the normative modeling was established using data from a single center, and this may not be generalized to other centers. Establishing multicenter modeling will be the next step..." "this study exclusively focused on schizophrenia patients. An increasing body of evidence implicates shared etiological and pathophysiological characteristics among mental disorders and, thus, it would be interesting for future studies to generalize our findings to other psychiatric disorders." "this result was exclusively based on inhibitory rTMS data. If excitatory rTMS were used, it is possible that the negative correlation of the atrophy map may predict better treatment outcomes."

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Atrophy network mapping approach adapted from lesion network mapping methodology; functional connectivity analysis using 652 healthy subjects' rs-fMRI data to map atrophy networks; W-map used as continuous weighted seed (not thresholded) for network mapping to avoid arbitrary threshold selection; specificity analysis comparing against 49 coordinate-based networks from non-psychiatric disorders (AD, FTD, CBS, PNFA); potential for personalized rTMS target selection from atrophy network.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: The study introduces 'atrophy network mapping' approach to link spatially heterogeneous individual-level structural abnormalities to a common functional network. The rTMS data came from a pre-existing randomized clinical trial (NCT02863094) that was not prospectively designed for this normative modeling study. For the independent healthy validation group (n=60): mean age ± SD = 25.3 ± 7.40, 34 women. The normative model uses a simple GLM rather than more sophisticated approaches (e.g., GAMLSS, GPR, HBR) used in other normative modeling studies, which the authors acknowledge as 'relatively rough but concise'. Functional connectivity data (rs-fMRI) from 652 of 797 healthy subjects were used for atrophy network mapping, not for the normative model itself.
